```{r upload PANDA data, include = FALSE}

##Read in cleaned PANDA data file
panda_raw <- read.csv(here::here("costly_data_s2.csv"), header = TRUE)
panda <- panda_raw[-c(1)]

```

```{r upload CMOM data, include = FALSE}

##Read in cleaned CMOM data file
cmom_raw <- read.csv(here::here("costly_data_s1.csv"), header = TRUE)
cmom <- cmom_raw

```

```{r make CMOM and PANDA data in alignment, include = FALSE}

##Change demo data to match PANDA

#Race
cmom <- cmom %>%
  mutate(race_bin = case_when(
    RacialEthno == "White" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Black" ~ "Black",
    RacialEthno == "Asian" ~ "Asian",
    RacialEthno == "Hispanic" ~ "Hispanic",
    RacialEthno == "African American" ~ "Black",
    RacialEthno == "White/Jewish" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "White/Caucasian" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "White/Colombian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "White/Asian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Puerto Rican/New Zealand" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Pakistani" ~ "Asian",
    RacialEthno == "Malaysian Chinese" ~ "Asian",
    RacialEthno == "Latino" ~ "Hispanic",
    RacialEthno == "Latina/Black" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Jewish" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Irish/Jewish" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Indian" ~ "Asian",
    RacialEthno == "Hispanish" ~ "Hispanic",
    RacialEthno == "Greek/Latin" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "European" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Dominician/Black" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Dominican and African American" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Cuaucasian" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Chinese/Caucasian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Chinese, Caucasian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Caucasian/Asian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Caucasian" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Cacuasian" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "British" ~ "White",
    RacialEthno == "Black/White/Cuban" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Black/Hispanic, Biracial" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Black/Dominican" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Black and Russian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Biracial" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Asian/White" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Asian/Caucasian" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Asian/Black" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "Asian Indian" ~ "Asian",
    RacialEthno == "Arab-American/Anglo" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "African American/Hispanic" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "AA/C/PR" ~ "Mixed",
    RacialEthno == "" ~ "NA"))

#Political ID
cmom <- cmom %>%
  mutate(Political_New = Political + 1)

#Mean center political ID
cmom$Political_New_C <- scale(cmom$Political_New, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
cmom$Political_New_C <- as.numeric(as.character(cmom$Political_New_C))

panda$pol_id_new_c <- scale(panda$pol_id_new, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
panda$pol_id_new_c <- as.numeric(as.character(panda$pol_id_new_c))

#Delete kids with NAs in pol ID column and condition column
panda <- panda %>%
  filter(!is.na(pol_id_new))

#Count how many people have spousal ideology variable data
sum(complete.cases(panda$pol_id_spouse))

#See correlation between between pol_id_new and pol_id_spouse
corr.test(panda$pol_id_new, panda$pol_id_spouse)

#Ceate variable to combine pol ID of parent 1 and spouse
panda$pol_id_2spouse <- rowMeans(subset(panda, select = c(pol_id_new, pol_id_spouse)))

#Create variable that incorporates polid_2spouse for 2 spouse families; otherwise pulls from pol_id_new
panda$pol_id_combo <- ifelse(is.na(panda$pol_id_spouse), panda$pol_id_new, panda$pol_id_2spouse)

#Check that new ar is calculated properly
check <- panda %>%
  select(ID, pol_id_new, pol_id_spouse, pol_id_2spouse, pol_id_combo)

#Check that we have the all participants with pol ID accounted for
sum(complete.cases(panda$pol_id_combo))

#Mean-center new var (combined pol ID of parent 1 and spouse)
panda$pol_id_combo_c <- scale(panda$pol_id_combo, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

#Make group assignment same as PANDA
cmom <- cmom %>%
  mutate(Group_New = factor(Group, labels = c("Ingroup", "Outgroup")))

panda <- panda %>%
  mutate(condition = factor(condition_group, labels = c("Ingroup, Outgroup")))

#Gender
cmom$Gender <- factor(cmom$Gender, levels = c("M", "F"))

#Delete CMOM kids without condition assignment
cmom <- cmom %>%
  filter(!is.na(Group_New))

##Condense dfs to relevant columns
cmom <- cmom %>%
  select(SID, Gender, race_bin, ExactAge, AgeC, YoungOld, SignPlacement, Badge, Group_New, Group, Version, Slide, WhoseBook, HardEasy, ThinkGetToGo, LessonCont, ImportantCont, ThinkYouGo, WishCont, SadCont, Recall, BadCont, TroubleCont, PlayWIth, NiceNot, WentDown, Political_New, Political_New_C, Authoritarian, Disciplinary, Fairness)

#Write .csv files
write.csv(panda, "costly_panda.csv")
write.csv(cmom, "costly_cmom.csv")

```

### PANDA sample

#### Child Demographics
```{r get demo info, include = FALSE}

#Create df with just kids who we have polID for (N = 181)
panda <- panda %>%
  filter(!is.na(pol_id_new))

#Age
psych::describe(panda$age)

#Gender
prop.table(xtabs(~gender, data = panda))

#Race
prop.table(xtabs(~race_bin, data = panda))

#Condition
xtabs(~condition_group, data = panda)

```

#### Parent Demographics
```{r prep parent demographic graphs panda, include = FALSE}

#Pol id (Parent 1)
psych::describe(panda$pol_id_new)
xtabs(~pol_id_new, data = panda)

#Pol id (combined)
psych::describe(panda$pol_id_combo)
xtabs(~pol_id_combo, data = panda)

```

#### Liking of video
```{r did kids like the video, include = FALSE}

#Liking video
prop.table(xtabs(~q_like_video_bin, data = panda)) 
prop.table(xtabs(~q_like_video_full, data = panda)) 

#Wanting to watch another video
prop.table(xtabs(~q_want_watch_bin, data = panda)) 
prop.table(xtabs(~q_want_watch_full, data = panda)) 

```

#### Comprehension Questions
```{r compute accuracy for comp questions, include = FALSE}

#Group membership comprehension

#Individual comprehension questions (1-4)
prop.table(xtabs(~group_correct, data = panda)) #94% correctly identified their own group membership
prop.table(xtabs(~target_correct, data = panda)) #98% correctly verified group of target (Stacy/Ethan)
prop.table(xtabs(~target_comp_correct, data = panda)) #95% correctly determined if they were in the same/different group as target
prop.table(xtabs(~liking_correct, data = panda)) #67% liked their own group most 

#Find average percentage across all 4 comprehension questions
comp_only <- data.frame(correct_all = c(panda[,"group_correct"], panda[,"liking_correct"], panda[,"target_correct"], panda[,"target_comp_correct"]))

#Overall comprehension
prop.table(xtabs(~correct_all, data = comp_only)) #89% correct overall

#Comprehension of transgression
prop.table(xtabs(~q_what_do, data = panda)) 
prop.table(xtabs(~q_nice_not_nice, data = panda)) 

#Opening/locking vid bank comprehension
prop.table(xtabs(~q_lock_comp, data = panda)) 
prop.table(xtabs(~q_open_comp, data = panda)) 

#Final comprehension question
prop.table(xtabs(~q_mancheck_remind, data = panda)) 

```

##### Check for moderation of comprehension qs by pol ID
```{r comp qs by pol ID, include = FALSE}

#What group are you a part of?
model_group_pol <- glm(group_correct ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_group_pol) #ns

#What group is the target a part of?
model_target_pol <- glm(target_correct ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_target_pol) #ns

#Are you guys in the same or a different group?
model_comp_pol <- glm(target_comp_correct ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_comp_pol) #ns

#Who do you like better?
model_like_pol <- glm(liking_correct ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_like_pol) #ns

#Comprehension of transgression
model_trans_pol <- glm(q_what_do ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_trans_pol) #ns

#Comprehension of nice/not nice
model_nicenot_pol <- glm(q_nice_not_nice ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_nicenot_pol) #ns

#Comprehension of lock function
model_lock_pol <- glm(q_lock_comp ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_lock_pol) #ns

#Comprehension of open function
model_open_pol <- glm(q_open_comp ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_open_pol) #ns

#Comprehension of open function
model_remind_pol <- glm(q_mancheck_remind ~ pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_remind_pol) #ns

```

#### Costly punishment decision
```{r descriptives for punishment choice, include = FALSE}

#Make punish_decide into factor
panda$q_punish_decideF <- as.factor(as.character(panda$q_punish_decide))

#Create new df with no NAs
panda_nona <- panda %>%
  filter(!is.na(q_punish_decide))

#Proportion of punishment (without NA)
prop.table(xtabs(~q_punish_decideF, data = panda_nona))

#Proportion of punishment (with NA)
panda[48] <- lapply(panda[48], addNA)
prop.table(xtabs(~q_punish_decideF, data = panda))

#Does age influence punishment?
model_punish_age <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_age)

```

#### Test for relation between desire to punish (non-costly) and costly  punishment
```{r exploratory analyses of costly and non-costly punishment, include = FALSE}

#Does children's belief that kid should get to watch the video affect punishment?
punish_getto <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ q_get_to_watch, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_getto)

#Add in age
punish_getto <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ q_get_to_watch*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_getto)

#Get means of children saying transgressor should get to watch video
punish_getto_summary <- panda %>%
    dplyr::summarize(q_get_to_watch_mean = mean(q_get_to_watch, na.rm = TRUE))
sd(panda$q_get_to_watch, na.rm = TRUE)

#Does ideology moderate this relation?
punish_getto_pol <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ q_get_to_watch*age_c*pol_id_new_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_getto_pol)

#Does condition moderate this relation?
punish_getto_cond <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ q_get_to_watch*age_c*condition_group, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_getto_cond)

```

#### Test for relation between validation measures and costly punishment
```{r probing validation questions, include = TRUE}

#Post-punishment questions

##1 - Happiness/sadness of transgressor after locking or leaving open
t.test(x = panda$q_feel_lock,
       y = panda$q_feel_open)

#Get SDs
panda <- panda %>%
  mutate(q_feel_all = case_when(
    !is.na(q_feel_lock) ~ q_feel_lock,
    !is.na(q_feel_open) ~ q_feel_open))

sd(panda$q_feel_all, na.rm = TRUE)

#Run as model
punish_feel <- lm(q_feel_all ~ q_punish_decide*age_c, data = panda)
summary(punish_feel)

##2 - Perceptions of what the transgressor will do next time? (1 = tear, 0 = hold)
punish_next <- glm(q_next_time ~ q_punish_decide*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_next)

#Re-code next time to reflect change in behavior; 1 = hold and 0 = tear
panda <- panda %>%
  mutate(change_behavior = 1 - q_next_time)

#Run with change behavior as variable
punish_change <- glm(change_behavior ~ q_punish_decide*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_change)

#Get means
(punish_change_summary <- panda %>%
    group_by(q_punish_decide) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(change_behavior_mean = mean(change_behavior, na.rm = TRUE)))

#Get sd
sd(panda$change_behavior, na.rm = TRUE)

##3 - Perception of why the transgressor acted how they did? (1 = bad person, 0 = bad day)
punish_why <- glm(q_person_day ~ q_punish_decide*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_why)

#Get means
(punish_why_summary <- panda %>%
    group_by(q_punish_decide) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(q_person_day = mean(q_person_day, na.rm = TRUE)))

#Get sd
sd(panda$q_person_day, na.rm = TRUE)

##4 - Desire to play with transgressor in the future? (0 = yes, 1 = no)
punish_play <- glm(q_play_with ~ q_punish_decide*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_play)

#Get means
(punish_play_summary <- panda %>%
    group_by(q_punish_decide) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(q_play_with = mean(q_play_with, na.rm = TRUE)))

#Get sd
sd(panda$q_play_with, na.rm = TRUE)

##5 - Perceptions of transgressor's remorse? (0 = yes, 1 = no)
punish_bad <- glm(q_feel_bad ~ q_punish_decide*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(punish_bad)

#Get means
(punish_bad_summary <- panda %>%
    group_by(q_punish_decide) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(q_feel_bad = mean(q_feel_bad, na.rm = TRUE)))

#Recode such that 1 = feels remorse
panda <- panda %>%
  mutate(q_feel_badyes = 1 - q_feel_bad)

#Get means
(punish_yesbad_summary <- panda %>%
    group_by(q_punish_decide) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(q_feelbadyes = mean(q_feel_badyes, na.rm = TRUE)))

```

#### Interaction and simple effects of CP by political ideology*group
```{r interaction and simple effects of CP, include = FALSE}

#Does punishment vary by condition, political ideology, and age?
model_punish_cond_pol_age <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_pol_age) 

#Check simple effects (within in- and out-group)
model_punish_cond_pol_age_simp <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group/pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_pol_age_simp) 

#Calculate pseudo-R2
PseudoR2(model_punish_cond_pol_age, c("Nagel"))

```

#### Follow up on 2-way interaction of CP: Johnson-Neyman technique
```{r follow up on 2-way cp interaction, include = FALSE}

#First, change condition to numeric variable (for J-N to run)
panda <- panda %>%
  mutate(condition_num = case_when(
    condition_group == "ingroup_toogit" ~ 0,
    condition_group == "outgroup_flurp" ~ 1,
  ))

#Re-run model with numeric condition variable and with pol_id_new not centered (for interpretability of graph)
model_punish_cond_pol_age_JN <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_num*pol_id_new*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_pol_age_JN) 

#J-N analysis code from other website
jn_panda <- johnson_neyman(
  model_punish_cond_pol_age_JN,
  condition_num,
  pol_id_new,
  vmat = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  plot = TRUE,
  control.fdr = FALSE,
  line.thickness = 0.5,
  df = "residual",
  digits = getOption("jtools-digits", 3),
  critical.t = NULL,
  sig.color = "#00BFC4",
  insig.color = "#F8766D",
  mod.range = c(1,7),
  title = "Johnson-Neyman plot: PANDA"
)
jn_panda

```

#### Interaction and simple effects of CP by political ideology*group (Parents 1 and 2; SOM)
```{r simple effects of CP, include = FALSE}

#Does punishment vary by condition, political ideology, and age?
model_punish_cond_polcombo_age <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*pol_id_combo_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_polcombo_age) 

#Check simple effects (within in- and out-group)
model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_simp <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group/pol_id_combo_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_simp) 

#Verify with filtering
model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_ingroup <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ pol_id_combo_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = subset(panda, condition_group == "ingroup_toogit"))
summary(model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_ingroup)

model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_outgroup <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ pol_id_combo_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = subset(panda, condition_group == "outgroup_flurp"))
summary(model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_outgroup)

#Calculate pseudo-R2
PseudoR2(model_punish_cond_polcombo_age, c("Nagel"))

```

#### Follow up on 2-way interaction of CP: Johnson-Neyman technique (Parents 1 and 2; SOM)
```{r follow up on 2-way cp interaction, include = FALSE}

#First, change condition to numeric variable (for J-N to run)
panda <- panda %>%
  mutate(condition_num = case_when(
    condition_group == "ingroup_toogit" ~ 0,
    condition_group == "outgroup_flurp" ~ 1,
  ))

#Return pol_id_combo to numeric
panda$pol_id_combo <- as.numeric(as.character(panda$pol_id_combo))

#Re-run model with numeric condition variable and with pol_id_new not centered (for interpretability of graph)
model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_JN <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_num*pol_id_combo*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_JN) 

#J-N analysis code from other website
jn_panda_combo <- johnson_neyman(
  model_punish_cond_polcombo_age_JN,
  condition_num,
  pol_id_combo,
  vmat = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  plot = TRUE,
  control.fdr = FALSE,
  line.thickness = 0.5,
  df = "residual",
  digits = getOption("jtools-digits", 3),
  critical.t = NULL,
  sig.color = "#00BFC4",
  insig.color = "#F8766D",
  mod.range = c(1,7),
  title = "Johnson-Neyman plot: PANDA"
)
jn_panda_combo

```

##### Plot punishment by political ideology*condition on CP (predicted)
```{r plot predicted means punishment, include = FALSE}

#Make labels for plot
pol_label7 <- c("1 \n Very \n liberal", "2", "3", "4","5", "6", "7 \n Very \n conservative")

#Reproduce model we're plotting (but without pol mean-centered)
model_punish_cond_pol_age1 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*pol_id_new*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_punish_cond_pol_age1) 

#Get predicted means
predicted_3way_panda <-effect("condition_group*pol_id_new*age_c",
                                    mod=model_punish_cond_pol_age1, confidence.level = .975)
predicted_3way_panda<-as.data.frame(predicted_3way_panda)

#Plot predicted means
plot_punish_pol_cond1_model <- ggplot() + 
  geom_jitter(data = panda, aes(x = pol_id_new, y = q_punish_decide, 
                  group = condition_group, color = condition_group), alpha = .7, height = .1) +
  stat_smooth(data = predicted_3way_panda, aes(x = pol_id_new, y = fit,
                                               group = condition_group, color = condition_group),
              method = "glm", method.args =list(family="binomial"), 
              fill = "#F6F3FF",
              se = TRUE,
              size = 2) +
  theme_classic() + 
  labs(x = "Parents' Political Ideology",  
  y ="Decision to Enact Costly Punishment\nAgainst Transgressor",
  color = "Transgressor's\nGroup") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                     labels = pol_label7) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")) + 
  geom_segment(aes(x = 1.65, y = .60, xend = 1.15, yend = .60), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5, "cm")), color = "#0E2EE4", size = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 6.00, y = .42, xend = 6.85, yend = .42), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5, "cm")), color = "#E40E0E", size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.726, linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2, color = "#0E2EE4") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5.889, linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2, color = "#E40E0E") +
    scale_color_manual(
    values = c("#8C8C8C", "#1F1F1F"),
    labels = c("Ingroup", "Outgroup")) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"))
plot_punish_pol_cond1_model

ggsave("figure5.pdf", width = 170, height = 100, units = "mm", dpi = 300)

```

#### Test for 2-way interaction on non-costly punishment
```{r test for effect on non-costly punishment, include = FALSE}

#Non-costly punishment (pre-costly paradigm)
model_getwatch_cond_pol_age <- glm(q_get_to_watch ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_getwatch_cond_pol_age) #ns

#Get means for non-costly punishment
(noncost_pun_summary <- panda %>%
  dplyr::summarize(q_get_to_watch = mean(q_get_to_watch, na.rm = TRUE)))

#Calculate SD
sd(panda$q_get_to_watch, na.rm = TRUE)

```

#### Test for 2-way interaction on beliefs about punishment
```{r test secondary questions, include = FALSE}

#Does time to punish vary by political ideology*condition?
model_time_cond_pol_age <- lm(q_punish_time ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c, data = panda)
summary(model_time_cond_pol_age) #no main or interactive effects

#Does the perception that the transgressor will transgress next time vary by condition*political ideology?
model_nexttime_cond_pol_age <- glm(q_next_time ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda)
summary(model_nexttime_cond_pol_age) #no main or interactive effects
```

```{r follow up on 2-way play with interaction, include = FALSE}
#First, change condition to numeric variable (for J-N to run)

    condition_group == "ingroup_toogit" ~ 0,

  ))

#J-N analysis code from other website
jn_panda_play <- johnson_neyman(
  model_playwith_cond_pol_age_JN,
  condition_num,
  pol_id_new,
  vmat = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  plot = TRUE,
  control.fdr = FALSE,
  line.thickness = 0.5,
  df = "residual",
  digits = getOption("jtools-digits", 3),
  critical.t = NULL,
  sig.color = "#00BFC4",
  insig.color = "#F8766D",
  mod.range = c(1,7),
  title = "Johnson-Neyman plot: PANDA"
)
jn_panda_play
```

#### Test ideology*condition interaction with neighborhood measures (by Zip)
```{r process and analyze zipcode data, include = FALSE}

#Change name to "zip"
colnames(panda)[colnames(panda) == "Zip.Code"] <- "zip"

#Trim df to just ID and zip
zip <- panda %>%
  select(ID, zip)
write.csv(zip, "costly5_zip.csv")

#Read in zipcode data
zip_raw <- read.csv(here::here("zip_code_data_s2.csv"), header = TRUE)
zip <- zip_raw

#Merge data
panda_zip <- merge(panda, zip_raw, by = c("ID", "zip"))

#Calculate population totals of minority diversity (i.e., all but White)
panda_zip <- panda_zip %>%
  mutate(tot.pop = tot_native_pop + tot_pacif_pop + tot_asian_pop + tot_black_pop + tot_hisp_pop + tot_other_pop + tot_white_pop) %>%
  mutate(tot.pop.div = 1 - (tot_white_pop / tot.pop))

panda_zip$tblack_0to10

#Rename columns as needed
colnames(panda_zip)[colnames(panda_zip) == "Fraction_College_Graduates_in_2012.16"] <- "frac_coll"
colnames(panda_zip)[colnames(panda_zip) == "Poverty_Rate_in_2012.16"] <- "pov_rate"
colnames(panda_zip)[colnames(panda_zip) == "Median_Rent_2012.16"] <- "med_rent"
colnames(panda_zip)[colnames(panda_zip) == "twhite_0to10"] <- "pro_white"
colnames(panda_zip)[colnames(panda_zip) == "tblack_0to10"] <- "pro_black"

#Test zipcode vars as covariates and predictors

#Total population
model_punish_totpop <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*total_population*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_zip)
summary(model_punish_totpop) #no 2-way interaction (p = .31)

model_punish_totpop_cov <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c + total_population, family = binomial, data = panda_zip)
summary(model_punish_totpop_cov) #2-way exists controlling for total pop (p = .011)

#Total population diversity
model_punish_popdiv <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*tot.pop.div*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_zip)
summary(model_punish_popdiv) #no 2-way interaction (.1466)

model_punish_popdiv_cov <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c + tot.pop.div, family = binomial, data = panda_zip)
summary(model_punish_popdiv_cov) #2-way exists, controlling for pop diversity (p = .0099)

#All college grad percentage
model_punish_colgrad <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*all_col_grad*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_zip)
summary(model_punish_colgrad) #no 2-way interaction (.947)

model_punish_colgrad_cov <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group*pol_id_new_c*age_c + all_col_grad, family = binomial, data = panda_zip)
summary(model_punish_colgrad_cov) #2-way exists, controlling for college grad (p = .018)
```

### Omnibus analyses (SOM)

#### Combine dfs
```{r create df for omnibus analyses, include = TRUE}

#Create new panda df to manipulate
panda_bind <- panda %>%
  mutate(cp = q_punish_decide,
         group = condition_group,
         pol = pol_id_new,
         age = age,
         SID = as.character(ID),
         study = 2)

#Recode condition column
panda_bind <- panda_bind %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    group == "ingroup_toogit" ~ "Ingroup",
    group == "outgroup_flurp" ~ "Outgroup"
    ))

#Condense to relevant columns
panda_bind <- panda_bind %>%
  select(SID, group, pol, age, cp, study)

#Create new cmom df to manipulate
cmom_bind <- cmom %>%
  mutate(cp = SignPlacement,
         group = Group_New,
         pol = 1.4*Political_New,
         age = ExactAge,
         SID = as.character(SID),
         study = 1)

#Condense to relevant columns
cmom_bind <- cmom_bind %>%
  select(SID, group, pol, age, cp, study)

#Create omni df of both frames
omni <- rbind(panda_bind, cmom_bind)

#Turn group into factor and cp into numeric
omni$group <- as.factor(omni$group)
omni$cp <- as.numeric(omni$cp)
omni$study <- as.factor(as.character(omni$study))

#Mean-center age variable
omni$age_c <- scale(omni$age, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) 

#Mean-center pol ideology variable
omni$pol_c <- scale(omni$pol, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) 

mean(omni$age, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(omni$pol, na.rm = TRUE)

```

#### Interaction and simple effects of CP by ideology*group
```{r run omnibus models, include = TRUE}

#Run model with study as interacting term
model_punish_omni_int <- glm(cp ~ group*pol_c*age_c*study, family = binomial, data = omni)
summary(model_punish_omni_int)

#Run model with study as covariate
model_punish_omni <- glm(cp ~ group*pol_c*age_c + study, family = binomial, data = omni)
summary(model_punish_omni)

#Check simple effects (within in- and out-group)
model_punish_omni_simp_ingroup <- glm(cp ~ pol_c*age_c + study, family = binomial, data = subset(omni, group == "Ingroup"))
summary(model_punish_omni_simp_ingroup) #ME for in-group

model_punish_omni_simp_outgroup <- glm(cp ~ pol_c*age_c + study, family = binomial, data = subset(omni, group == "Outgroup"))
summary(model_punish_omni_simp_outgroup) #no ME for out-group

#Calculate pseudo-R2
PseudoR2(model_punish_omni, c("Nagel"))

```

#### Follow up on 2-way interaction: Johnson-Neyman technique
```{r follow up on 2-way interaction at SDs panda omni, include = TRUE}

#First, change condition to numeric variable (for J-N to run)
omni <- omni %>%
  mutate(group_num = case_when(
    group == "Ingroup" ~ 0,
    group == "Outgroup" ~ 1,
  ))

#Re-run model with numeric condition variable and with pol_id_new not centered (for interpretability of graph)
model_punish_omni_JN <- glm(cp ~ group_num*pol*age_c + study, family = binomial, data = omni)
summary(model_punish_omni_JN)

#J-N analysis code from other website
jn_omni <- johnson_neyman(
  model_punish_omni_JN,
  group_num,
  pol,
  vmat = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  plot = TRUE,
  control.fdr = FALSE,
  line.thickness = 0.5,
  df = "residual",
  digits = getOption("jtools-digits", 3),
  critical.t = NULL,
  sig.color = "#00BFC4",
  insig.color = "#F8766D",
  mod.range = c(1,7),
  title = "Johnson-Neyman plot: Omni"
)
jn_omni #on both sides of plot

```

##### Plot punishment by political ideology*condition on CP (predicted)
```{r plot predicted means punishment omni, include = TRUE}

#Make labels for plot
pol_label7 <- c("1 \n Very \n liberal", "2", "3", "4","5", "6", "7 \n Very \n conservative")

#Reproduce model we're plotting (but without pol mean-centered)
model_punish_omni <- glm(cp ~ group*pol*age_c + study, family = binomial, data = omni)
summary(model_punish_omni)

#Get predicted means
predicted_3way_omni<-effect("group*pol*age_c",
                                    mod=model_punish_omni, confidence.level = .975)
predicted_3way_omni<-as.data.frame(predicted_3way_omni)

#Plot predicted means with logistic look
plot_punish_pol_cond_omni <- ggplot() + 
  geom_jitter(data = omni, aes(x = pol, y = cp, 
                  group = group, color = group), alpha = .4, height = .1) +
  stat_smooth(data = predicted_3way_omni, aes(x = pol, y = fit,
                                               group = group, color = group),
              method = "glm", method.args =list(family="binomial"), 
              fill = "#BFBEC3",
              se = TRUE) +
  theme_classic() + 
  labs(x = "Parents' Political Ideology",  
  y ="Decision to Enact Costly Punishment\nAgainst Transgressor",
  color = "Transgressor's\n Group") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                     labels = pol_label7) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1.450, 4.675), linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(
    values = c("#1a8cff", "#ff884d"),
    labels = c("Ingroup", "Outgroup")) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10))

```
